purpose: Pimozide is used to help control motor and vocal tics in people with Tourette syndrome, especially when other treatments have not worked well enough. It helps reduce the sudden, uncontrolled movements or sounds that come with this condition. It is usually considered when tics are seriously affecting daily life.
how_it_works: Pimozide works by blocking certain chemical messengers in the brain called dopamine receptors. Dopamine is a substance that helps send signals between nerve cells, and when it is overactive, it can contribute to tics. By calming down this overactivity, pimozide helps reduce the frequency and severity of tics.
common_side_effects: You may feel drowsy or tired, especially when you first start taking it. Other common effects include dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, dizziness, weight gain, and difficulty urinating. Some people also notice muscle stiffness or restlessness.
warnings: Pimozide can affect your heart rhythm, causing a serious change called QT prolongation, so your doctor will monitor your heart with regular EKGs. It should never be combined with certain antibiotics, antifungals, or other medicines that also affect heart rhythm. Do not suddenly stop taking it without talking to your doctor first. Rare but serious side effects include a condition called tardive dyskinesia, which causes uncontrolled facial movements, and a rare emergency called neuroleptic malignant syndrome causing high fever and muscle rigidity.
typical_dosing: Adults and children over 12 typically start at a low dose of 1 to 2 mg per day, taken by mouth, and the dose is slowly increased based on how well it works and how well it is tolerated. The usual maintenance dose is between 7 and 16 mg per day, but doses above 10 mg per day are used cautiously. Your doctor will find the lowest dose that controls your symptoms effectively.
